newsitem.title: USA: MobileMedia enters $200 mln loan pact.
newsitem.headline: MobileMedia enters $200 mln loan pact.

text.p: MobileMedia Corp on Monday said it entered into a debtor-in-possession loan agreement with Chase Manhattan Corp for up to $200 million in financing.

MobileMedia, which has filed for protection under Chapter 11 of the U.S. Bankruptcy Code, named a corporate turnaround consultant, Joseph Bondi, as a chairman of the company's restructuring and Ronald Grawert as chief executive officer.
The company also entered into pacts with certain key suppliers, including Motorola Inc, Glenayre Technologies Inc and NEC Corp.
Its request to pay the pre-petition claims of each of these suppliers was approved by the bankruptcy court on February 6, the company said.
MobileMedia said it had placed orders with Motorola, the company's largest supplier of pagers and Glenayre, its largest supplier of infrastructure equipment.

MobileMedia said as a result of its agreements with Motorola, Glenayre and the other suppliers, it could now borrow up to $70 million under the DIP facility. It said it had already used $48 million of that amount to pay suppliers.
A court hearing for final approval of the DIP financing was scheduled for February 19, the company said.
Assuming final approval was granted at that hearing, the company said it would gain access to another $30 million of DiP funds for a total of $100 million.
The remaining $100 million of DIP funds would become available on May 1, if MobileMedia's business plan was approved by the banks' financial adviser, it said.

With regard to the restructuring appointments, David Bayer had been acting CEO and would remain chairman, the company said. Bondi is a managing director with Alvarez & Marsal, a turnaround consulting firm, and has been a consultant with MobileMedia since December 1996, it said.
